real_qa.q: Why did Waymo suspend its partnership with Uber in Phoenix after initially launching together?
real_qa.r: Waymo suspended the partnership with Uber in Phoenix, but users could still book directly through the Waymo app. The first time the speaker rode an autonomous car, it was through Waymo's native app rather than Uber. Waymo has now developed their app fully and operates independently in multiple cities.
real_qa.requete: Waymo Uber partnership Phoenix suspended why

real_qa.q: In which cities is Waymo currently operating autonomous vehicles as of this episode?
real_qa.r: Waymo operates in San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Las Vegas, Denver, Dallas, San Antonio, Houston, Nashville, Orlando, Tampa, and Miami. They are also expanding into London and Japan as foreign markets.

real_qa.q: Why did Waymo initially partner with Uber instead of launching independently in Phoenix?
real_qa.r: The partnership allowed Waymo to get quicker access to users. Since Waymo had a large user base but no ride-share offering, partnering with Uber let them get people in and out of vehicles. Once they developed their native app and expanded their technology to handle various weather conditions, they no longer needed Uber's platform.
real_qa.requete: Waymo Uber partnership reason user access

real_qa.q: How has Waymo's autonomous vehicle technology evolved to handle weather conditions beyond sunny skies?
real_qa.r: Waymo initially operated only in sunny parts of the lower United States because their vehicles would pull over during sandstorms and rain. They have now solved the weather problem, allowing them to expand into northern parts of the United States where snow and rain are common.
